newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hold up in face of Nikkei rise.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hold up in face of Nikkei rise.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures remained resilient in the face of hefty gains in Tokyo stocks on Friday as most players were confident Japan would maintain a low interest rate regime for the time being, dealers said.

Overnight comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that Japan was overly pessimistic about its economy spurred active buying of stocks, pushing the Nikkei average of leading shares up by 465.97 points to close at 18,330.01.
But the effect on interest rate markets was tempered by Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita's statement early in the day that Japan would maintain its easy monetary policy.
"The Nikkei went up sharply but there was almost no reaction in Euroyen because every participant thinks the low interest rates will continue," said a trader at a Japanese house.
Dealers said activity in Euroyen futures was being hampered by the fact that the market had priced in steady rates until the third quarter and was unsure of the outlook beyond that.
"December Euroyen's been in a two- to three-tick range. It's very difficult to push the contract higher from here," said a Japanese bank dealer.
Dealers said December Euroyen was likely to remain in a 99.15-99.25 range for the foreseeable future. It was quoted at 99.20 at 1110 GMT against its IMM close at 99.19.
March JGBs settled at 126.37 against their previous 126.30.
Eurodollar futures edged up on follow-through buying after a firm finish in Chicago where players were reassured by Greenspan's market-friendly speech to the Senate Finance Committee.
Dealers said interest would be focused on the U.S. fourth quarter Gross Domestic Product, due to be released at 1330 GMT.
September Eurodollars finished at 94.06 against their IMM close at 94.04 on volume of 5,800 lots.
